messages:
marta: heads up — saw a spike in OOMs on prod-serving-2 at ~02:00 UTC. pattern looks like high-concurrency decode jobs + large KV prefill. putting initial traces here for context.

ryan: ugh. do we have profiler data or heap-snapshots?

marta: pasting quick profiler summary below (shortened):

```
hotspots:
  - workspace allocations: 48% (many 8-32KB churn)
  - slab fragmentation: ~23% unusable free due to many small allocs
  - kv-prefill allocations: bursty during decode windows
  - decoder kernel time: normal
  - concurrency spikes correlate with long seqs (>=1024)

note: no kernel regressions in perf profile, looks mem-layout + allocator behavior.
```

jen: thanks. so likely not a kernel selection issue directly, more allocator + kv sizing?

zach: yeah — also saw increased batch sizes in the routing logs which increases prefill pressure. if batching heuristics route bigger requests to the same worker we blow slabs.

sam: quick triage idea: reduce per-request kv-prefill cap from 128 -> 32 for a canary pool, enable workspace reuse for decode path, and trigger slab compaction more aggressively under pressure. low-risk rollback.

marta: i like that. can we add a short throttling guard during prefill to avoid >X concurrent prefill ops per GPU? basically per-gpu semaphore.

ryan: yes. even a token-bucket on prefill calls would smooth bursts. implementable in ~1h for canary.

sam: pushed a patch to the canary branch with the `--kv-prefill-max=32 --kv-prefill-concurrency=4` flags and workspace-reuse enabled. command for rollout: `./deploy canary --pool=prod-serving-2 --flags kv-prefill-max=32,kv-prefill-concurrency=4`

opsbot: deploybot: canary deploy started for prod-serving-2 by sam at 1925679200. watch logs: <https://go/redwood/logs/prod-serving-2/canary>

zach: we should also track fragmentation metric (slab_free_fragmentation) and add an alert if >20% for 5m. current alert thresholds too high.

jen: agreed. add a short-term dashboard with prefills/sec, kv-cache-hits, slab_fragmentation, prefill_concurrency. link it in the ticket.

marta: recorded action items: 1) canary rollout with kv caps (sam) 2) token-bucket prefill throttle if canary helps (ryan) 3) alert + dashboard for fragmentation (zach) 4) postmortem + longer-term allocator tuning (marta) — please ack and add ETA.

sam: ack. canary up, watching. will report in 20m.

ryan: ack. i'll prototype token-bucket today, PR by EOD.

zach: ack. i'll add alert + dashboard by tomorrow morning.

jen: ETA for postmortem and allocator proposal?

marta: aim for draft by Fri — we need to evaluate: slab compaction heuristics, micro-chunk coalescing, and opportunistic buffer reuse across prefills.

sam: initial canary numbers: prefill rate down ~5x per-request, OOM count dropped to 0 in the canary pool for the last 25m. will collect longer windows but promising. :tada:

ryan: nice. if stable we should backfill to other pools and consider making prefill-cap adaptive based on slab_fragmentation signal.

marta: yes — adaptive cap + batching-aware routing (avoid bundling many long-seq prefillers) is the longer-term fix. opened ticket: <https://go/redwood/T12345> with notes and next steps.

sam: logging snippet for the throttling behavior (canary):

```
[2026-03-18T02:10:05Z] prefill_request: req=cbf2 id=... size=512 -> capped to 32 entries, queued by token-bucket (wait_ms=12)
[2026-03-18T02:10:08Z] workspace_reuse: hit=true reuse_ms=1.2
[2026-03-18T02:10:08Z] slab_frag: 18.2%
```

marta: great. keep rolling and document perf numbers in the ticket. once we validate, next patch is allocator-side: reduce min slab class to handle many 8-32KB live objects and enable micro-coalescing on free.

jen: +1. also include regression tests that simulate high-concurrency long-seq traffic in our perf harness. otherwise we might ship and regress again.

zach: will add a perf test in the harness: `harness/evict_prefill_stress.py` that steps prefill sizes, concurrency, and checks fragmentation + OOM rates.

marta: thanks team. i'll close this thread after we confirm canary 2h stable. postmortem draft to follow.

sam: current status (1925679509): canary 2h stable, no OOMs, fragmentation trending down. moving to roll to prod-serving-1 next if no surprises.

ryan: sweet. closing loop in T12345 and will follow up with token-bucket PR.

opsbot: deploybot: rollout to prod-serving-1 scheduled by sam at 1925679600.

marta: closing for now. thanks all.
